sanskrit: ubhau varāyudhadharāv ubhau raṇakṛtaśramau ubhau ca bāhuśabdena nādayantau nabhastalam
english: Both bore the finest weapons, both were seasoned in the toil of battle, and both made the vault of heaven resound with the clamor of their arms.

sanskrit: ubhau viśrutakarmāṇau pauruṣeṇa balena ca ubhau ca sadṛśau yuddhe śambarāmararājayoḥ
english: Both were renowned for their deeds, in manhood and in might, and both were equals in war to Śambara and to the king of the gods.

sanskrit: kārtavīryasamau yuddhe tathā dāśaratheḥ samau viṣṇuvīryasamau vīrye tathā bhavasamau yudhi
english: In battle they were the peers of Kārtavīrya, and the equals of the son of Daśaratha; in valor they matched the might of Viṣṇu, and in combat they were the equals of Bhava.

sanskrit: ubhau śvetahayau rājan rathapravaravāhinau sārathī pravarau caiva tayor āstāṃ mahābalau
english: Both had white horses, O king, and both rode in the finest of chariots; and the charioteers of each were peerless and of mighty strength.

sanskrit: tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahārāja rājamānau mahārathau siddhacāraṇasaṃghānāṃ vismayaḥ samapadyata
english: Beholding those two great warriors in their splendor, O mighty king, wonder took hold of the hosts of the Siddhas and the Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrās tataḥ karṇaṃ sabalā bharatarṣabha parivavrur mahātmānaṃ kṣipram āhavaśobhinam
english: Then the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra with their forces, O bull of the Bharatas, swiftly closed in around the great-souled Karṇa, resplendent in the fray.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā hṛṣṭā dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ parivavrur mahātmānaṃ pārtham apratimaṃ yudhi
english: In the same way the Pāṇḍavas, exultant and led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, closed in around the great-souled Pārtha, who had no equal in battle.

sanskrit: tāvakānāṃ raṇe karṇo glaha āsīd viśāṃ pate tathaiva pāṇḍaveyānāṃ glahaḥ pārtho 'bhavad yudhi
english: In the battle, O lord of peoples, Karṇa was the stake of your men, just as Pārtha was the stake of the Pāṇḍavas in the fight.

sanskrit: ta eva sabhyās tatrāsan prekṣakāś cābhavan sma te tatraiṣāṃ glahamānānāṃ dhruvau jayaparājayau
english: They themselves were there as the assembled members of the gaming-court and became its spectators; and for those two who staked their lives, victory and defeat hung in the balance.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ dyūtaṃ samāyattaṃ vijayāyetarāya vā asmākaṃ paṇḍavānāṃ ca sthitānāṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: Upon those two the dicing turned, for victory or for the other lot, as we and the Pāṇḍavas stood ranged at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: tau tu sthitau mahārāja samare yuddhaśālinau anyonyaṃ pratisaṃrabdhāv anyonyasya jayaiṣiṇau
english: Those two stood firm in the battle, O great king, skilled in war, each enraged against the other, each seeking the other's defeat.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau prajihīrṣetām indravṛtrāv ivābhitaḥ bhīmarūpadharāv āstāṃ mahādhūmāv iva grahau
english: Both longed to strike each other down on every side, like Indra and Vṛtra; terrible of form, they stood like two great smoke-wreathed planets of ill omen.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe sākṣepā vivādā bharatarṣabha mitho bhedāś ca bhūtānām āsan karṇārjunāntare vyāśrayanta diśo bhinnāḥ sarvalokāś ca māriṣa
english: Then in the sky, O bull of the Bharatas, there arose taunting wrangles and mutual divisions among the beings over Karṇa and Arjuna; the quarters were split, my lord, and all the worlds took different sides.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvāḥ piśācoragarākṣasāḥ pratipakṣagrahaṃ cakruḥ karṇārjunasamāgame
english: Gods, Dānavas, and Gandharvas, Piśācas, serpents, and Rākṣasas took up opposing partisanships at the encounter of Karṇa and Arjuna.

sanskrit: dyaur āsīt karṇato vyagrā sanakṣatrā viśāṃ pate bhūmir viśālā pārthasya mātā putrasya bhārata
english: The heaven with its constellations was intent on Karṇa's side, O lord of peoples; while the broad earth was for Pārtha, O Bhārata, as a mother for her son.

sanskrit: saritaḥ sāgarāś caiva girayaś ca narottama vṛkṣāś cauṣadhayas tatra vyāśrayanta kirīṭinam
english: The rivers and the oceans, and the mountains too, O best of men, the trees and the herbs—all there took the side of the Diademed One.

sanskrit: asurā yātudhānāś ca guhyakāś ca paraṃtapa karṇataḥ samapadyanta khecarāṇi vayāṃsi ca
english: The Asuras and the Yātudhānas and the Guhyakas, O scorcher of foes, together with the birds that range the sky, took their stand on Karṇa's side.

sanskrit: ratnāni nidhayaḥ sarve vedāś cākhyānapañcamāḥ sopavedopaniṣadaḥ sarahasyāḥ sasaṃgrahāḥ
english: All the jewels and the treasures, and the Vedas with their tales for a fifth, together with the Upavedas and Upaniṣads, the secret doctrines and the digests—

sanskrit: vāsukiś citrasenaś ca takṣakaś copatakṣakaḥ parvatāś ca tathā sarve kādraveyāś ca sānvayāḥ viṣavanto mahāroṣā nāgāś cārjunato 'bhavan
english: Vāsuki and Citrasena, Takṣaka and Upatakṣaka, and all the mountains too, and the sons of Kadrū with their lineages—the venom-bearing serpents of great wrath—took their place on Arjuna's side.

sanskrit: airāvatāḥ saurabheyā vaiśāleyāś ca bhoginaḥ ete 'bhavann arjunataḥ kṣudrasarpās tu karṇataḥ
english: The serpents of Airāvata's race, the sons of Surabhi, and the Vaiśāleyas—these stood on Arjuna's side, while the lesser snakes were for Karṇa.

sanskrit: īhāmṛgā vyāḍamṛgā maṅgalyāś ca mṛgadvijāḥ pārthasya vijayaṃ rājan sarva evābhisaṃśritāḥ
english: The wolves and beasts of prey, and the auspicious creatures, beasts and birds—all of these, O king, looked to Pārtha's victory and cleaved to it.

sanskrit: vasavo marutaḥ sādhyā rudrā viśve 'śvinau tathā agnir indraś ca somaś ca pavanaś ca diśo daśa dhanaṃjayam upājagmur ādityāḥ karṇato 'bhavan
english: The Vasus, the Maruts, the Sādhyas, the Rudras, the Viśvedevas and the two Aśvins, Agni and Indra and Soma and the Wind, and the ten quarters—these came to Dhanaṃjaya, while the Ādityas stood on Karṇa's side.

sanskrit: devās tu pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ sagaṇārjunato 'bhavan yamo vaiśravaṇaś caiva varuṇaś ca yato 'rjunaḥ
english: The gods, together with the ancestors and their hosts, sided with Arjuna; and Yama and Vaiśravaṇa and Varuṇa stood where Arjuna stood.

sanskrit: devabrahmanṛparṣīṇāṃ gaṇāḥ pāṇḍavato 'bhavan tumburupramukhā rājan gandharvāś ca yato 'rjunaḥ
english: The hosts of the divine, brahmin, royal, and human seers were on the Pāṇḍava's side; and the Gandharvas led by Tumburu, O king, were where Arjuna was.

sanskrit: prāveyāḥ saha mauneyair gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ īhāmṛgavyāḍamṛgair dvipāś ca rathapattibhiḥ
english: The Prāveyas together with the Mauneyas, the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases, along with the wolves and beasts of prey, the elephants, and the chariot-riders and foot-soldiers—

sanskrit: uhyamānās tathā meghair vāyunā ca manīṣiṇaḥ didṛkṣavaḥ samājagmuḥ karṇārjunasamāgamam
english: Borne aloft thus by the clouds and the wind, the wise ones came together, eager to behold the encounter of Karṇa and Arjuna.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvā nāgā yakṣāḥ patatriṇaḥ maharṣayo vedavidaḥ pitaraś ca svadhābhujaḥ
english: Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, serpents, Yakṣas, and winged beings, the great seers learned in the Vedas, and the ancestors who feed on the funeral offering—

sanskrit: tapo vidyās tathauṣadhyo nānārūpāmbaratviṣaḥ antarikṣe mahārāja vinadanto 'vatasthire
english: Austerities, sciences, and the healing herbs, robed and gleaming in their varied forms, took their stand in the sky, O great king, crying aloud.

sanskrit: brahmā brahmarṣibhiḥ sārdhaṃ prajāpatibhir eva ca bhavenāvasthito yānaṃ divyaṃ taṃ deśam abhyayāt
english: Brahmā, together with the brahmin-seers and the Prajāpatis, attended by Bhava, came in a celestial car to that place.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā prajāpatiṃ devāḥ svayaṃbhuvam upāgaman samo 'stu deva vijaya etayor narasiṃhayoḥ
english: Seeing the Lord of creatures, the Self-existent, the gods drew near and said: "O god, let the victory of these two lions among men be even."

sanskrit: tad upaśrutya maghavā praṇipatya pitāmaham karṇārjunavināśena mā naśyatv akhilaṃ jagat
english: Hearing this, Maghavat bowed to the Grandsire and said: "Let not the whole world be destroyed through the ruin of Karṇa and Arjuna.

sanskrit: svayaṃbho brūhi tad vākyaṃ samo 'stu vijayo 'nayoḥ tat tathāstu namas te 'stu prasīda bhagavan mama
english: O Self-existent One, speak the word: let the victory of these two be equal. So let it be—homage to you; be gracious to me, O Lord."

sanskrit: brahmeśānāv atho vākyam ūcatus tridaśeśvaram vijayo dhruva evāstu vijayasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then Brahmā and Īśāna spoke this word to the lord of the thirty gods: "Let the victory belong assuredly to the great-souled Vijaya.

sanskrit: manasvī balavāñ śūraḥ kṛtāstraś ca tapodhanaḥ bibharti ca mahātejā dhanurvedam aśeṣataḥ
english: He is high-minded, strong, and brave, accomplished in arms, rich in austerity; and the mighty-splendored one wields the whole science of archery without exception.

sanskrit: atikramec ca māhātmyād diṣṭam etasya paryayāt atikrānte ca lokānām abhāvo niyato bhavet
english: By his greatness of soul he might overstep what fate ordains for him, through some turn of events; and were that overstepped, the destruction of the worlds would surely follow.

sanskrit: na vidyate vyavasthānaṃ kṛṣṇayoḥ kruddhayoḥ kva cit sraṣṭārau hy asataś cobhau sataś ca puruṣarṣabhau
english: There is nowhere any withstanding the two Kṛṣṇas when they are wroth; for both of these bulls among men are the creators of what is not and of what is.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇāv etau purāṇāv ṛṣisattamau aniyattau niyantārāv abhītau sma paraṃtapau
english: These two are Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the ancient and most excellent of seers; uncontrolled themselves, they are the controllers of all, fearless and scorchers of the foe.

sanskrit: karṇo lokān ayaṃ mukhyān prāpnotu puruṣarṣabhaḥ vīro vaikartanaḥ śūro vijayas tv astu kṛṣṇayoḥ
english: Let this Karṇa, the bull among men, attain the foremost worlds—the hero Vaikartana, the brave; but let the victory be the two Kṛṣṇas'.

sanskrit: vasūnāṃ ca salokatvaṃ marutāṃ vā samāpnuyāt sahito droṇabhīṣmābhyāṃ nākaloke mahīyatām
english: And let him win a place in the world of the Vasus, or of the Maruts, and, together with Droṇa and Bhīṣma, be honored in the world of heaven."

sanskrit: ity ukto devadevābhyāṃ sahasrākṣo 'bravīd vacaḥ āmantrya sarvabhūtāni brahmeśānānuśāsanāt
english: Thus addressed by the two gods of gods, the Thousand-eyed spoke his word, calling upon all beings by the command of Brahmā and Īśāna:

sanskrit: śrutaṃ bhavadbhir yat proktaṃ bhagavadbhyāṃ jagaddhitam tat tathā nānyathā tad dhi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ gatamanyavaḥ
english: "You have heard what the two Lords have spoken for the good of the world. So shall it be and not otherwise—so let your anger pass, and abide in peace."

sanskrit: iti śrutvendravacanaṃ sarvabhūtāni māriṣa vismitāny abhavan rājan pūjayāṃ cakrire ca tat
english: Hearing Indra's words thus, all beings, my lord, were filled with wonder, O king, and did honor to that decree.

sanskrit: vyasṛjaṃś ca sugandhīni nānārūpāṇi khāt tathā puṣpavarṣāṇi vibudhā devatūryāṇy avādayan
english: And from the sky the gods let fall showers of fragrant flowers of varied kinds, and sounded the celestial drums.

sanskrit: didṛkṣavaś cāpratimaṃ dvairathaṃ narasiṃhayoḥ devadānavagandharvāḥ sarva evāvatasthire rathau ca tau śvetahayau yuktaketū mahāsvanau
english: Eager to behold the matchless single combat of those two lions among men, the gods, Dānavas, and Gandharvas all took their stations; and those two chariots, white-horsed, with banners set and loud of sound, drew on.

sanskrit: samāgatā lokavīrāḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak vāsudevārjunau vīrau karṇaśalyau ca bhārata
english: The heroes of the world, come together, blew their conches each apart—the valiant Vāsudeva and Arjuna, and Karṇa and Śalya, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad bhīrusaṃtrāsakaraṃ yuddhaṃ samabhavat tadā anyonyaspardhinor vīrye śakraśambarayor iva
english: Then there arose that battle, terrifying to the timid, between the two who vied in valor, like that of Śakra and Śambara.

sanskrit: tayor dhvajau vītamālau śuśubhāte rathasthitau pṛthagrūpau samārchantau krodhaṃ yuddhe parasparam
english: The two banners of those warriors, garlandless, shone forth as they stood upon the chariots, each of a different form, and they seemed to rouse each other's wrath in the fight.

sanskrit: karṇasyāśīviṣanibhā ratnasāravatī dṛḍhā puraṃdaradhanuḥprakhyā hastikakṣyā vyarājata
english: Karṇa's banner, like a venomous serpent, set with the essence of jewels, firm, resembling Purandara's bow, an elephant-girth, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: kapiśreṣṭhas tu pārthasya vyāditāsyo bhayaṃkaraḥ bhīṣayann eva daṃṣṭrābhir durnirīkṣyo ravir yathā
english: But Pārtha's emblem, the foremost of apes, with gaping jaws and terrible, struck fear with its fangs, hard to look upon as the sun.

sanskrit: yuddhābhilāṣuko bhūtvā dhvajo gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ karṇadhvajam upātiṣṭhat so 'vadīd abhinardayan
english: Eager for battle, the banner of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva drew near to Karṇa's banner, and it spoke, roaring out loud.

sanskrit: utpatya ca mahāvegaḥ kakṣyām abhyahanat kapiḥ nakhaiś ca daśanaiś caiva garuḍaḥ pannagaṃ yathā
english: Springing up with great force, the ape struck at the elephant-girth with its claws and teeth, as Garuḍa falls upon a serpent.

sanskrit: sukiṅkiṇīkābharaṇā kālapāśopamāyasī abhyadravat susaṃkruddhā nāgakakṣyā mahākapim
english: Adorned with fair little bells, of iron like the noose of Death, the serpent-girth, sorely enraged, rushed upon the great ape.

sanskrit: ubhayor uttame yuddhe dvairathe dyūta āhṛte prakurvāte dhvajau yuddhaṃ pratyaheṣan hayān hayāḥ
english: As the supreme single combat of the two was joined like a game of dice, the two banners waged their own war, and the horses neighed defiance at the horses.

sanskrit: avidhyat puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ śalyaṃ nayanasāyakaiḥ sa cāpi puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ tathaivābhisamaikṣata
english: The Lotus-eyed one pierced Śalya with the arrows of his glance, and he in turn looked back upon the Lotus-eyed one just so.

sanskrit: tatrājayad vāsudevaḥ śalyaṃ nayanasāyakaiḥ karṇaṃ cāpy ajayad dṛṣṭyā kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: There Vāsudeva overcame Śalya with the arrows of his eyes, and Kuntī's son Dhanaṃjaya likewise overcame Karṇa with his gaze.

sanskrit: athābravīt sūtaputraḥ śalyam ābhāṣya sasmitam yadi pārtho raṇe hanyād adya mām iha karhi cit kim uttaraṃ tadā te syāt sakhe satyaṃ bravīhi me
english: Then the charioteer's son, speaking to Śalya with a smile, said: "If Pārtha should slay me here in battle today by any chance, what would then be your course thereafter? Tell me truly, my friend."

sanskrit: śalya uvāca yadi karṇa raṇe hanyād adya tvāṃ śvetavāhanaḥ ubhāv ekarathenāhaṃ hanyāṃ mādhavapāṇḍavau
english: Śalya said: "If today, O Karṇa, the White-horsed one should slay you in battle, then I myself, with this one chariot, would slay both Mādhava and the Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam eva tu goviṃdam arjunaḥ pratyabhāṣata taṃ prahasyābravīt kṛṣṇaḥ pārthaṃ param idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: In just this way did Arjuna speak in turn to Govinda; and Kṛṣṇa, laughing, said this further word to Pārtha:

sanskrit: pated divākaraḥ sthānāc chīryetānekadhā kṣitiḥ śaityam agnir iyān na tvā karṇo hanyād dhanaṃjayam
english: "The maker of day might fall from his place, the earth might shatter into many pieces, fire might turn cold—but Karṇa will not slay you, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: yadi tv evaṃ kathaṃ cit syāl lokaparyasanaṃ yathā hanyāṃ karṇaṃ tathā śalyaṃ bāhubhyām eva saṃyuge
english: But if such a thing should somehow come to pass, like the overturning of the worlds, then I myself would slay Karṇa, and Śalya too, with my bare arms in the battle."

sanskrit: iti kṛṣṇavacaḥ śrutvā prahasan kapiketanaḥ arjunaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ kṛṣṇam akliṣṭakāriṇam mamāpy etāv aparyāptau karṇaśalyau janārdana
english: Hearing Kṛṣṇa's words, the ape-bannered Arjuna, laughing, replied to Kṛṣṇa, the tireless doer of deeds: "Even both of them, Karṇa and Śalya, are no match for me, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: sapatākādhvajaṃ karṇaṃ saśalyarathavājinam sacchatrakavacaṃ caiva saśaktiśarakārmukam
english: Karṇa with his pennon and banner, with Śalya and his chariot and steeds, with his parasol and armor, with his spear, arrows, and bow—

sanskrit: draṣṭāsy adya śaraiḥ karṇaṃ raṇe kṛttam anekadhā adyainaṃ sarathaṃ sāśvaṃ saśaktikavacāyudham na hi me śāmyate vairaṃ kṛṣṇāṃ yat prāhasat purā
english: Today you shall see Karṇa cut to pieces by my arrows in the battle—him, with his chariot, his steeds, his spear, his armor, and his weapons; for my enmity finds no rest, since once he laughed aloud at Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: adya draṣṭāsi govinda karṇam unmathitaṃ mayā vāraṇeneva mattena puṣpitaṃ jagatīruham
english: Today, O Govinda, you shall see Karṇa torn down by me, as a flowering forest tree is torn down by a maddened elephant.

sanskrit: adya tā madhurā vācaḥ śrotāsi madhusūdana adyābhimanyujananīm anṛṇaḥ sāntvayiṣyasi kuntīṃ pitṛṣvasāraṃ ca saṃprahṛṣṭo janārdana
english: Today, O slayer of Madhu, you shall hear those sweet words; today, freed of my debt, you shall comfort Abhimanyu's mother and Kuntī, your father's sister, with great gladness, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: adya bāṣpamukhīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ sāntvayiṣyasi mādhava vāgbhiś cāmṛtakalpābhir dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Today, O Mādhava, you shall comfort tear-faced Kṛṣṇā, and with words like nectar shall comfort the king of righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tad devanāgāsurasiddhasaṃghair; gandharvayakṣāpsarasāṃ ca saṃghaiḥ brahmarṣirājarṣisuparṇajuṣṭaṃ; babhau viyad vismayanīyarūpam
english: Saṃjaya said: Thronged with the hosts of gods and serpents, Asuras and Siddhas, and with the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Apsarases, frequented by brahmin-seers and royal-seers and the bird-king's kin, the heaven shone with a form to fill one with wonder.

sanskrit: nānadyamānaṃ ninadair manojñair; vāditragītastutibhiś ca nṛttaiḥ sarve 'ntarikṣe dadṛśur manuṣyāḥ; khasthāṃś ca tān vismayanīyarūpān
english: Resounding with sweet cries, with the music of instruments and song and hymns of praise and dances, all the men gazed up into the sky and beheld those sky-dwelling forms wondrous to look upon.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ kurupāṇḍuyodhā; vāditrapatrāyudhasiṃhanādaiḥ ninādayanto vasudhāṃ diśaś ca; svanena sarve dviṣato nijaghnuḥ
english: Then the warriors of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, exultant, with the din of instruments, the rustle of feathered shafts, and lion-roars, made the earth and the quarters resound, and with that uproar all of them fell upon their foes.

sanskrit: nānāśvamātaṅgarathāyutākulaṃ; varāsiśaktyṛṣṭinipātaduḥsaham abhīrujuṣṭaṃ hatadehasaṃkulaṃ; raṇājiraṃ lohitaraktam ābabhau
english: Crowded with the swarm of countless horses, elephants, and chariots, unbearable with the rain of fine swords, spears, and lances, frequented by the fearless and heaped with slain bodies, the field of battle shone red with blood.

sanskrit: tathā pravṛtte 'strabhṛtāṃ parābhave; dhanaṃjayaś cādhirathiś ca sāyakaiḥ diśaś ca sainyaṃ ca śitair ajihmagaiḥ; parasparaṃ prorṇuvatuḥ sma daṃśitau
english: As the rout of the weapon-bearers thus set in, Dhanaṃjaya and the son of Adhiratha, both armored, veiled the quarters and the host, and each other, with their sharp, straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: tatas tvadīyāś ca pare ca sāyakaiḥ; kṛte 'ndhakāre vividur na kiṃ cana bhayāt tu tāv eva rathau samāśrayaṃs; tamonudau khe prasṛtā ivāṃśavaḥ
english: Then, when darkness was wrought by the arrows of your men and of the foe, they could discern nothing; but out of fear all took refuge in those two chariots alone, the dispellers of gloom, like the rays of light spread out in the sky.

sanskrit: tato 'stram astreṇa parasparasya tau; vidhūya vātāv iva pūrvapaścimau ghanāndhakāre vitate tamonudau; yathoditau tadvad atīva rejatuḥ
english: Then those two scattered each other's missile with their own, like the winds of east and west; and amid the thick-spread darkness, dispellers of gloom, they shone exceedingly bright, like two risen suns.

sanskrit: na cābhimantavyam iti pracoditāḥ; pare tvadīyāś ca tadāvatasthire mahārathau tau parivārya sarvataḥ; surāsurā vāsavaśambarāv iva
english: "These two are not to be assailed"—so urged, the foe and your men alike then stood still, ringing those two great warriors about on every side, as gods and Asuras ring Vāsava and Śambara.

sanskrit: mṛdaṅgabherīpaṇavānakasvanair; ninādite bhārata śaṅkhanisvanaiḥ sasiṃhanādau babhatur narottamau; śaśāṅkasūryāv iva meghasaṃplave
english: While the air rang with the sound of tabors, kettledrums, cymbals, and drums, O Bhārata, and with the blare of conches, those two best of men, roaring like lions, shone forth like the moon and the sun amid a gathering of clouds.

sanskrit: mahādhanurmaṇḍalamadhyagāv ubhau; suvarcasau bāṇasahasraraśminau didhakṣamāṇau sacarācaraṃ jagad; yugāstasūryāv iva duḥsahau raṇe
english: Both standing within the circle of their great bows, both full of splendor, with a thousand arrow-rays for beams, as if longing to burn up the world of moving and unmoving things, they were unbearable in battle, like two suns set at the age's end.

sanskrit: ubhāv ajeyāv ahitāntakāv ubhau; jighāṃsatus tau kṛtinau parasparam mahāhave vīravarau samīyatur; yathendrajambhāv iva karṇapāṇḍavau
english: Both unconquerable, both destroyers of the enemy, those two accomplished warriors sought to slay each other; in the great battle the two best of heroes, Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava, met like Indra and Jambha.

sanskrit: tato mahāstrāṇi mahādhanurdharau; vimuñcamānāv iṣubhir bhayānakaiḥ narāśvanāgān amitau nijaghnatuḥ; parasparaṃ jaghnatur uttameṣubhiḥ
english: Then those two wielders of great bows, loosing mighty missiles with their fearful shafts, the matchless pair slew men, horses, and elephants, and struck at each other with their finest arrows.

sanskrit: tato visasruḥ punar arditāḥ śarair; narottamābhyāṃ kurupāṇḍavāśrayāḥ sanāgapattyaśvarathā diśo gatās; tathā yathā siṃhabhayād vanaukasaḥ
english: Then, tormented again by the arrows of those two best of men, the followers of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas scattered, with their elephants, foot-soldiers, horses, and chariots, and fled to the quarters, even as forest creatures flee in terror of the lion.

sanskrit: tatas tu duryodhanabhojasaubalāḥ; kṛpaś ca śāradvatasūnunā saha mahārathāḥ pañca dhanaṃjayācyutau; śaraiḥ śarīrāntakarair atāḍayan
english: Then Duryodhana, the Bhoja, and the son of Subala, and Kṛpa together with the son of Śaradvat—those five great warriors—smote Dhanaṃjaya and Acyuta with arrows that make an end of the body.
